claims.claim: He was blind from early childhood and spent his life teaching in Alexandria, Egypt.
The three‑book treatise On the Trinity (De Trinitate) has traditionally been ascribed to Didymus but its authorship is now widely disputed.
The text draws on Cyril of Alexandria’s anti‑Arian theology and cites mid‑fifth‑century sources on Arians, Macedonians and Eunomians, showing it was written after those controversies.
The discovery of the Toura papyri and comparison with Didymus’s authentic commentaries have led many scholars to consider De Trinitate an anonymous work rather than a genuine composition of Didymus.
